title: 01 Matrix: Distance to Nearest Zero
contract: For a nonempty rectangular binary matrix containing at least one zero, return each cell's Manhattan distance to its nearest zero.
brute: int rows=grid.length,cols=grid[0].length;int[][] out=new int[rows][cols];for(int r=0;r<rows;r++)for(int c=0;c<cols;c++){int best=Integer.MAX_VALUE;for(int x=0;x<rows;x++)for(int y=0;y<cols;y++)if(grid[x][y]==0)best=Math.min(best,Math.abs(x-r)+Math.abs(y-c));out[r][c]=best;emit("Compare against every zero","cell",new int[]{r,c},"distances",out);}return out;
optimal: int rows=grid.length,cols=grid[0].length;int[][] out=new int[rows][cols];Deque<int[]> q=new ArrayDeque<>();for(int r=0;r<rows;r++)for(int c=0;c<cols;c++){out[r][c]=-1;if(grid[r][c]==0){out[r][c]=0;q.add(new int[]{r,c});}}while(!q.isEmpty()){int[] cell=q.remove();for(int[] d:DIRS){int r=cell[0]+d[0],c=cell[1]+d[1];if(r>=0&&r<rows&&c>=0&&c<cols&&out[r][c]<0){out[r][c]=out[cell[0]][cell[1]]+1;q.add(new int[]{r,c});}}emit("Propagate shortest distances from all zeroes","cell",cell,"distances",out);}return out;
reasoning: With no obstacles, distance between two cells is Manhattan distance; compare each cell with every zero.
Start all zeroes at distance zero and expand a single shared BFS frontier.
The first discovery gives the nearest source distance. A per-cell BFS repeats exploration unnecessarily. If obstacles were introduced, the baseline Manhattan formula would no longer be valid.
